purpose: Preserve nonrepresentative mixed-platform creator income reports with exact source families, denominator limitations and zero-earner uncertainty.

studies.title: Creator Earnings Report 2025
studies.independence_note: Influencer Marketing Hub is a partner/syndicator of the same NeoReach report, not a second independently sampled dataset.
studies.sampled_population: Cross-platform creators recruited for an industry survey; full recruitment frame and response rate unavailable.
studies.platform_scope: multiple social and creator platforms, not YouTube-only
studies.verification_of_earnings: self-reported; no audited income statements documented on public summary
studies.geographic_denominator: worldwide claimed survey outreach, geography weighting not established
studies.observation_period: report 2025; exact respondent earnings reference window and fieldwork dates not disclosed on public overview
studies.earning_definition: annual creator earnings as reported; whether gross receipts versus profit cannot be established from source overview
limitations: Sampling is not probability-based from all creator or YouTube accounts.
YouTube membership or activity of respondents does not isolate their YouTube-native payouts.
A result marketed as a monetization barrier does not establish a universal causal threshold.
Survey respondents with income are not a first-year entrant cohort.
The same source family appears in partner publications and must not be counted twice.

studies.title: Creator Spotlight 2025 Monetization Report
studies.independence_note: Original newsletter reader survey; independent from the NeoReach/IMH source family.
studies.sampled_population: Adult creator subscribers to an engaged newsletter, mainly in North America; mix of video, newsletter, podcast and social creators.
studies.invitation_description: Nearly 300,000 most-engaged subscribers (not an exact exposure or response denominator).
studies.earning_definition: self-reported calendar-year creator-work earnings, not confirmed net business profit
limitations: The responding audience is self-selected newsletter subscribers, not the population of YouTube uploaders.
Nearly half is qualitative and must not be silently converted to a precise percentage.
The approximate invitation count is not an exact number of survey recipients or reliable probability-sample response denominator.
Six-figure earners across mixed creator businesses cannot predict YouTube ad payments.
Observational revenue-diversification patterns are associations, not proven earnings causes.

studies.title: The State of Creators 2026
studies.independence_note: One survey of 5,095 creators reported on its original research page and in the associated press release; not multiple respondent datasets.
studies.sampled_population: Respondents contacted through Influencers.club creator research across reported 100 regions; no probability frame or response-rate denominator established on public report.
studies.platform_scope: Creators working across platforms including Instagram, TikTok and YouTube; not a YouTube-only sample
studies.data_collection_mode: Commercial creator survey with vendor-enriched creator profile and platform metadata
studies.verification_of_earnings: Creator income responses are survey-reported; enrichment of demographic or platform data does not demonstrate independent auditing of respondent income
studies.geographic_denominator: 100 reported countries or regions; selection and weighting not shown to represent global creator population
studies.observation_period: Survey fieldwork May 29 to June 29, 2026, asking annual creator income over the previous year
studies.earning_definition: Annual creator income reported by respondents; native payouts vs sponsors, expenses and taxes not separately verified
studies.margin_of_error_verifiability: Publisher reports ±1.4 points; probability-sampling basis and design-based confidence interpretation not established on public page. Do not use as global/YouTube statistical uncertainty.
limitations: CreatorIQ/Influencers.club runs commercial creator services and industry surveys, not a population census.
Recruitment and response probabilities, subgroup denominators and global population weights are not sufficiently documented for probability-based inference.
The published ±1.4 percentage-point margin of error must not be presented as verified probability-based confidence for all creators.
Creator earnings span multiple platforms, revenue streams and maturity levels; they are not native YouTube payouts or newcomer profit.
The source's 67% and 62% figures refer to survey respondents, not to all YouTube creators or all people who attempted to publish.

studies.title: The Creator Revolution: 2023 Factworks 20-country creator survey
studies.lead_organization: Factworks (Meta-commissioned); report by Creative Class Group
studies.independence_note: One independently fielded Factworks study under a Meta commission, published by Creative Class Group in December 2024. Original 20-country and US results are overlapping respondent populations; large-US group supplements phase 2 and is not an independent survey family.
studies.sampled_population: Original-content publishers with >=1000 followers on at least one social platform, sampled through internet-user surveys in 20 countries; excludes many beginning and abandoned creator attempts
studies.platform_scope: Mixed-platform creator activity and revenues; not YouTube-only nor all people who attempted to start creating
studies.data_collection_mode: 2023 multistage commissioned internet-user questionnaire plus separate US large-creator supplementation; creator respondent demographics weighted within countries and countries equally combined
studies.verification_of_earnings: Respondent self-report of annual content-creator revenue, no bank verification, no consistent cost or tax reconciliation
studies.geographic_denominator: 20 named countries, global percentages computed by report weighting; US subset separately reported
studies.observation_period: 2023 fieldwork measuring reported creator revenues annually; exact income recall dates and item denominators not supplied
studies.earning_definition: Creator activity revenue across social media platforms before demonstrated production costs, taxes and net-profit reconciliation
limitations: The study's creator definition requires >=1000 followers on some platform; zero-revenue responses do not include true zero-follower entrants or all attempted new YouTube channels.
Twenty countries and US/large-US categories have different, overlapping cohorts; their percentages cannot be pooled or treated as a within-channel transition.
Meta commissioned the study; independently gathered self-reported revenues may be affected by selection, disclosure, recall and sponsorship context.
The additional 207 large US creator observations were merged with appropriate subsets of the original US respondents; 12% is not an independent worldwide creator cohort.
Revenue is not after-expense profit, nor YouTube ad payouts; individual response item denominators and bank-level reconciliation are not available.

comparability.supported: Discuss direction of income inequality and survey-selection limitations across different creator samples.
comparability.method: Do not pool a 2025 cross-platform earnings share with 2018/2021/2024 Patreon observations or a 297-channel already-monetized YouTube cohort; populations, channels, years, methods and currency denominators differ. CreatorIQ's separate 2026 mixed-platform vendor survey is an additional respondent dataset, but not evidence of a platform-specific representative earnings distribution.

publication_rules: Preserve all source-family IDs to avoid duplicate studies.
Do not present a multi-platform respondent percentage as a YouTube frequency.
Do not interpret zero monetization as zero production costs or no work.
Use null for unknown exact sample sizes, exact proportions, and revenue distributions.
Do not infer sensitive demographic attributes of individual creators.
